objective: Pick up the blue block using all available MIM ARM resources and operator assistance as needed.
current_pose_note: open claw, low visual search pose after relocalization sweep
what_mim_learned_this_pass: Servo 4 hand side-to-side strongly changes gripper presentation; useful zone around 80-90.
Servo 3 wrist turn around 65-75 gives better gripper angle than prior 89 for this block position.
Base 90-96 can approach the block center-hole path, but the block slides away unless mechanically captured first.
Symmetric pinch is weak for this cube; center-hole hook or deeper bracket is more promising.
High lift before secure capture causes loss; lift must remain incremental and validated.
why_operator_help_is_now_useful: The block has shifted outside the current reliable grip lane during exploration.
Blind continued movements would mostly push the block rather than improve capture.
A quick reposition lets MIM test the learned wrist/hand alignment instead of rediscovering the block location.
operator_reposition_request: Place the blue block directly between the two claw tips in the current open pose, with the large center hole facing the left claw tip if possible. Leave a small gap so the tips can close around/through the hole without immediately pushing the block away.
next_mim_action_after_reposition: Use wrist=65, hand-side=80 as starting alignment.
Use C12 offset when the sensor beam is aligned: estimated tip clearance = raw distance - 123mm.
Close in stages and inspect at each stage.
Lift only to elbow 42, then 46, then 50 after visible retention.
Use table-height RPLIDAR diff to check whether block leaves the table plane.
